title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Calculation of the Guaranty Carried Forward on an Assumed Loan
content:
When a veteran selling a home to a buyer who assumes the VA loan asks to be released from liability, the release records the guaranty that stays in force on the loan for the assuming buyer. Under the VA Home Loan Guaranty, the guaranty that stays in force is the guaranty on the loan record, rounded to the cent.

## How the figure is built

The guaranty follows the loan's balance at the rate the guaranty on the record bears to the original loan amount, so it never exceeds the guaranty issued against the veteran's entitlement. The figure recorded is the balance figured, times the guaranty on the record divided by the original loan amount, times each of the three shares divided by one hundred, rounded to the cent once at the end.

| Element | In this calculation | Record read |
|---|---|---|
| Balance figured | The original loan amount | The loan record (loan amount) |
| Rate | The guaranty on the record divided by the original loan amount | The loan record (guaranty, loan amount) |
| Cure share | 100 | — |
| Assumption-timing share | 100 | — |
| Repeat-claim share | 100 | — |

With the balance figured equal to the original loan amount and each share at 100, the figure recorded equals the guaranty on the loan record, rounded to the cent. Nothing is rounded until the last multiplication is made.

## Worked figures (hypothetical loans)

**Loan 1.** Original loan amount 300,000.00; guaranty on the record 75,000.00. Balance figured 300,000.00; times 75,000.00 divided by 300,000.00 gives 75,000.00; times 100, 100 and 100 each divided by one hundred leaves 75,000.00. The guaranty that stays in force is 75,000.00 dollars.

**Loan 2.** Original loan amount 212,345.67; guaranty on the record 53,086.42. The figure recorded is 212,345.67 times 53,086.42 divided by 212,345.67, which is 53,086.42, rounded to the cent once at the end: 53,086.42 dollars.
